mainTopic: Court rules and punishments for a בן נח, and when a non-Jew who sins with Jewish עריות is judged by Jewish law
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a ruling from the previous amud. A ברייתא then lists the special court rules for a בן נח: one judge, one witness, no התראה, a man and not a woman, and even a relative. רבי ישמעאל adds that a בן נח is executed even for killing a fetus. רב יהודה draws all of these rules from בראשית 9:5. The fetus rule comes from reading 'באדם' as 'a person inside a person', while תנא דבי מנשה reads the same word as teaching חנק. The גמרא then answers questions about women: they are excluded from judging, but a בת נח is still executed for murder and for adultery. Next, a ברייתא learns from 'איש איש' that a non-Jew who sins with Jewish עריות is judged by Jewish law. רבי יוחנן explains that this means a נערה המאורסה, and a later step adds a woman who entered חופה without relations. Finally the גמרא begins to question רבי מאיר's rule linking a בן נח's עריות to Jewish death penalties, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line: he is executed for it
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier discussion: the person is executed for the killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is executed for killing him.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish the ruling from the end of the previous discussion. The person is put to death for the killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new topic. It is the end of a ruling about a killer, which applies to a בן נח as well. Once it is finished, the גמרא moves on to a new ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: For him, meaning for killing him

phrases.english: He is executed for him.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from before this section; 'for him' means for killing that person.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶהֱרָג עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the previous sugya that runs into this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The killer in the earlier case is liable to death.

steps.title: A ברייתא: how a בן נח is judged
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אחא found a source saying that a בן נח can be executed by one judge, on one witness, with no warning. The judge or witness must be a man, but he may be a relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא found it written in a book of אגדתא from the house of רב: a בן נח is executed by one judge and on the word of one witness, without התראה. The testimony must come from a man and not from a woman. Even a relative may testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a written teaching listing the court rules for a בן נח. These rules are much easier than the rules for judging a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew needs a full בית דין, two witnesses, and התראה before he can be executed. A בן נח needs none of these. There is one limit in the other direction: a woman cannot serve as the judge or the witness. A relative, however, can.

keyTerms.meaning: A book of אגדה (teachings), kept in the study hall
Of the house (study hall) of רב
A descendant of Noah, meaning a non-Jew
A warning given before the sin, which is needed to execute a Jew

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a בן נח is judged more strictly in every way. Fewer judges and witnesses are needed, but a woman still cannot be the judge or the witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section explains where each of these rules comes from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Acha found

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה כְּתִיב בְּסֵפֶר אַגַּדְתָּא דְּבֵי רַב:
phrases.english: that it was written in a book of Aggada of the house of Rav:
A descendant of Noah is executed by one judge,
and by one witness, without forewarning,
by the mouth of a man and not by the mouth of a woman,
and even a relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכַּח רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא דַּהֲוָה כְּתִיב בְּסֵפֶר אַגַּדְתָּא דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is executed by one judge, on one witness, without התראה. The judge or witness must be a man, and may be a relative.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: even for killing a fetus
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said that a בן נח is executed even for killing a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: even for fetuses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule, quoted in the name of רבי ישמעאל. A בן נח is executed even for killing an unborn baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now moves from how a בן נח is judged to what he is liable for. Killing a fetus does not make a Jew liable to death, but רבי ישמעאל holds that it does make a בן נח liable. The גמרא gives the source for this rule in step 8.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael they said:
Even for fetuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule to the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is liable to death for killing a fetus.

steps.title: Where do these rules come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rules listed in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source teaches these rules for a בן נח. This question sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these rules is very different from the rules for a Jew, so the גמרא wants a source in the פסוקים. It is asking for information, not attacking the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's rules
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the court rules for a בן נח

steps.title: רב יהודה: the פסוק teaches one judge
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes בראשית 9:5. The word 'I will require' teaches that even one judge is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: the verse says, 'And surely your blood of your lives I will require.' This teaches that even one judge is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by pointing to the פסוק God told נח about killing. He begins with the rule of one judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verb אדרש, 'I will require,' is said in the singular. רב יהודה learns from this that one person can demand justice for the killing, so one judge is enough. The next words of the same פסוק will teach the other rules.

keyTerms.meaning: I will require, I will demand an accounting (singular)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Because the verse says,
'And surely your blood of your lives I will require,'
even by one judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בראשית 9:5; the singular 'אדרש' teaches that one judge is enough

steps.title: The rest of the פסוק teaches the other rules
steps.stepSummary: Each later phrase in the פסוק teaches another rule: no התראה, one witness, a man and not a woman, and even a relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the hand of every animal' teaches that he is executed even without warning. 'I will require it, and from the hand of man' teaches that even one witness is enough. 'From the hand of a man' teaches that a woman cannot serve. 'His brother' teaches that even a relative can serve.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה goes through the rest of the פסוק phrase by phrase. He matches each phrase to one of the rules in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts killing by an animal next to killing by a man, and an animal obviously gets no warning, so no התראה is needed. The singular 'אדרשנו' teaches that one witness is enough. 'איש' teaches that a man is needed, not a woman, and 'אחיו' teaches that even a relative may serve.

keyTerms.meaning: From the hand of every animal
His brother, used here to mean a relative

steps.whatToRemember: All the court rules for a בן נח come from one פסוק, בראשית 9:5. 'I will require' teaches one judge. 'Every animal' teaches no התראה. 'I will require it' teaches one witness. 'Man' teaches not a woman. 'His brother' teaches even a relative.

phrases.english: 'From the hand of every animal,'
even without forewarning.
'I will require it; and from the hand of man,'
even by one witness.
'From the hand of a man,' and not from the hand of a woman.
'His brother,' even a relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד כׇּל חַיָּה אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּהַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's reading of the same פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each phrase of בראשית 9:5 is the source for one rule in the ברייתא

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's source for the fetus ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבי ישמעאל's ruling about fetuses and asks where it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said that a בן נח is executed even for killing fetuses. What is רבי ישמעאל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי ישמעאל's ruling from earlier and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 finished explaining the sources for the other rules in the list. Now the גמרא turns to the one rule still left: רבי ישמעאל's addition about killing a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason? (asks for the source)

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael they said:
even for fetuses.
What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of the other rules in the list to רבי ישמעאל's extra rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that a בן נח is executed for killing a fetus.

steps.title: The fetus is 'a person inside a person'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'באדם' in בראשית 9:6 is read as 'a person inside a person', which means a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'One who sheds the blood of a person, in a person, his blood shall be shed.' Which person is inside a person? You must say this is a fetus in its mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי ישמעאל's source. He reads the words 'הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם' together as 'a person who is inside a person', which means a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בָּאָדָם' can mean 'by a person' or 'in a person'. רבי ישמעאל attaches it to the first half of the פסוק, so the פסוק says: whoever sheds the blood of a person who is inside a person, his blood shall be shed. That makes killing a fetus a capital crime for a בן נח.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sheds a person's blood (a murderer)
In a person / by a person
You must say (only one answer fits)

phrases.english: For it is written:
"One who sheds the blood of a person,
in a person, his blood shall be shed."
Which person is inside a person?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה עוּבָּר שֶׁבִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: You must say: this is a fetus in its mother's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading 'הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם' as 'a person inside a person' teaches that killing a fetus is a capital crime for a בן נח.

steps.title: The תנא קמא reads 'באדם' as teaching strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא follows the school of מנשה: he attaches 'באדם' to the end of the פסוק and learns that a בן נח is executed by חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא is the תנא of the school of מנשה, who says that every death penalty for בני נח is only strangulation. He moves the word 'in a person' to the end of the פסוק and reads it this way: 'In a person his blood shall be shed.' What shedding of a person's blood stays inside the person's body? You must say: this is strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא did not list fetuses. He uses the same word 'בָּאָדָם' for a different lesson: how a בן נח is executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל attaches 'בָּאָדָם' to the first half of the פסוק, so it teaches about a fetus. The תנא דבי מנשה attaches it to the second half: 'in a person his blood shall be shed', meaning the blood stays inside the body. That describes חנק, so all death penalties for בני נח are strangulation. Since he uses the word for this, he has no source left for the fetus ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study house of מנשה
Throw it onto the end of the פסוק (attach the word to the second half)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use the same word 'בָּאָדָם'. The disagreement is only about which half of the פסוק the word belongs to.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one word can be read two ways, and how that difference creates a real argument in הלכה.

phrases.english: And the first tanna
is the tanna of the school of Menashe,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כׇּל מִיתָה הָאֲמוּרָה לִבְנֵי נֹחַ
phrases.english: who says: every death penalty stated for the descendants of Noah
is only strangulation,
and he moves this word "in a person"
onto the end of the verse,
and he interprets it like this:
"In a person his blood shall be shed" —
what shedding of a person's blood
stays inside the person's body?
phrases.notes: Blood that is 'shed' but never leaves the body: the person dies without bleeding outside.

phrases.english: You must say: this is strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא תַּנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the other opinion does not accept the reading in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא uses 'בָּאָדָם' to teach that a בן נח is executed by חנק, so it does not teach about a fetus.

steps.title: רב המנונא: isn't a woman also commanded about justice?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges the rule that only a man can judge or testify for a בן נח, citing the פסוק about אברהם's household.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objects: Is a woman not commanded? But it is written: 'For I have known him, so that he will command his sons and his household after him... to do righteousness and justice'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks the rule from step 6 that a בן נח is judged by a man and not a woman. He argues from a פסוק that women were also commanded to do justice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אברהם will command 'his sons and his household' to do 'צדקה ומשפט'. 'His household' includes the women, so it seems women are also commanded in משפט. If so, why can't a woman judge or testify?

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raises an objection:
And is a woman not commanded?
But isn't it written:
"For I have known him, so that he will command, etc."!
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:19. The rest of the פסוק says 'his sons and his household... to do righteousness and justice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא: וְאִשָּׁה לָא מִפַּקְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fetus topic and goes back to the rule that the judge or witness must be a man.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a בן נח is judged or testified against by a man and not a woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'His household' in the פסוק includes women, and the פסוק includes 'משפט', so women seem to be commanded in justice too.

steps.title: Sons for justice, household for charity
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers himself: 'his sons' goes with justice, and 'his household' goes with charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he resolved it: 'His sons' were commanded about justice, and 'his household' about charity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers his own question. He splits the פסוק, so each group gets a different command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two groups and two commands. The sons go with משפט (justice), and the household, meaning the women, goes with צדקה (charity). So the פסוק does not prove women are commanded about judging, and the rule from step 6 stands.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He asked it and he answered it himself

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל reads 'באדם' as a fetus; the תנא דבי מנשה reads it as חנק. Women are excluded from judging a בן נח because in אברהם's פסוק the household (the women) was commanded about צדקה, not דין.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raises the objection and he resolves it:
"His sons" — for justice,
"his household" — for charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the פסוק: each group gets its own command.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sons and household were commanded about justice, so women would be fit to judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the sons were commanded about justice; the household (the women) was commanded about charity, so the rule excluding women stands.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jewish woman who kills is not executed
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא סבא suggests that since the פסוק says 'מיד איש' (from the hand of a man), a בת נח who murders should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא the Elder said to רב פפא: Why not say that a non-Jewish woman who killed is not executed? The פסוק says 'from the hand of a man,' not 'from the hand of a woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא challenges the death penalty for a non-Jewish woman who murders. He points out that the פסוק only mentions a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' has just been used to limit some of the rules of בני נח to men. רב אויא pushes the same reading further. If 'איש' leaves out women in those cases, maybe it leaves out women from the punishment for murder too.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אויא the Elder, the one asking the questions
A daughter of Noah, meaning a non-Jewish woman
Why not say...? (a word that brings up a possible reading)
From the hand of a man

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Avya the Elder said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא בַּת נֹחַ שֶׁהָרְגָה לֹא תֵּיהָרֵג,
phrases.english: Say that a daughter of Noah who killed should not be executed,
since "at the hand of a man" is written, and not "at the hand of a woman"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא לְרַב פָּפָּא: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea that 'איש' means men only and applies it to the murder law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The death penalty for a בת נח who murders
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'איש', which should leave out women.

steps.title: Anyone who sheds blood is included
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers in the name of רב יהודה: 'שופך דם האדם' covers every killer, man or woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said: 'One who sheds the blood of a person' means in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers from the next פסוק. It speaks about anyone who sheds blood, without saying 'man'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שופך דם האדם' describes the killer by what he does, not by whether he is a man or a woman. So it includes women, even though the earlier phrase said 'איש'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sheds the blood of a person
In any case, with no exceptions

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Yehuda said:
"One who sheds the blood of a person" means in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a different phrase in the פסוקים that is general
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מיד איש' leaves women out of the punishment for murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שופך דם האדם' includes every killer, so a בת נח who murders is executed.

steps.title: Maybe a non-Jewish woman who commits adultery is not executed
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא tries again: the פסוק about marriage says 'יעזב איש' (a man shall leave), so maybe a woman is not punished for adultery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say that a non-Jewish woman who committed adultery is not executed? The פסוק says 'Therefore a man shall leave,' and not a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא asks the same kind of question about adultery. He uses the פסוק that the איסור for בני נח is learned from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of adultery for בני נח comes from the פסוק about a man cleaving to his wife. That פסוק opens by speaking of a man. So maybe only the man is held responsible, and not the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore a man shall leave (his father and mother)

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בַּת נֹחַ שֶׁזִּינְּתָה לֹא תֵּיהָרֵג,
phrases.english: Say: a daughter of Noah who committed adultery should not be executed,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב ״עַל כֵּן יַעֲזׇב אִישׁ״ וְלֹא אִשָּׁה?
phrases.english: as it is written: "Therefore a man shall leave," and not a woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: בַּת נֹחַ שֶׁזִּינְּתָה לֹא תֵּיהָרֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question built the same way as step 12, this time about adultery.
steps.kashyaTarget: The death penalty for a בת נח who commits adultery
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source פסוק speaks of 'איש', which should leave out women.

steps.title: The פסוק joins man and woman together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers in the name of רב יהודה: the end of the פסוק, 'and they shall be one flesh', puts both of them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said: 'And they shall be one flesh.' The פסוק then joined them together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers from the end of the same פסוק, which speaks of the man and the woman together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק starts with the man, but it ends with 'they' becoming one flesh. That ending includes both of them, so the woman is included in the איסור and its punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall be one flesh
The פסוק then mixed them together (included both)

steps.whatToRemember: Both times, 'איש' does not exempt a בת נח. Another phrase in the same פסוקים includes women, both for murder and for adultery.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Yehuda said:
"And they shall be one flesh":
the verse then combined them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: ״וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the end of the same פסוק, which includes both
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יעזב איש' means only the man is held responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והיו לבשר אחד' includes the woman, so a בת נח who commits adultery is executed.

steps.title: The double 'איש איש' includes non-Jews in עריות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the double word 'איש איש' that non-Jews are forbidden in עריות just like Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The פסוק could have said 'a man.' Why does it say 'a man, a man'? To include non-Jews, who are warned about forbidden relations just like Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. A ברייתא uses the extra word 'איש' in the פסוק about עריות to include non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'איש' would have been enough to teach the איסור to Jews. The extra 'איש' is read as adding people who would not have been included otherwise, and those people are the non-Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say...?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "A man" would be enough,
so why does the verse say "a man, a man"?
To include the non-Jews,
who are warned about forbidden relations like Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אִישׁ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: where the איסור עריות for non-Jews comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra 'איש' teaches that non-Jews are forbidden in עריות like Jews.

steps.title: We already learned this from 'לאמר'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we already learned the איסור עריות for non-Jews from 'לאמר', so why do we need 'איש איש'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it learned from here? It is learned from there: 'saying' refers to forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The same rule was already learned from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word 'לאמר' in the command to אדם הראשון was read as hinting to עריות. Since that already teaches the איסור for all people, the extra 'איש' looks unnecessary for this purpose. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it learned from here?
Saying, a word from the command to אדם

phrases.english: But is it derived from here?
It is derived from there!
"Saying": this refers to forbidden relations.
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:16. This was learned on the previous daf, in the list of the seven מצוות of בני נח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא? מֵהָתָם נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used by the ברייתא in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'איש איש' as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already known from 'לאמר', so this second source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two verses, two kinds of forbidden women
steps.stepSummary: 'לאמר' teaches the איסור for the non-Jews' own עריות. 'איש איש' teaches the איסור for Jewish עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the verse is talking about their forbidden relations. Here, it is talking about our forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 17: each source teaches a different case, so neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לאמר' covers the women forbidden to a non-Jew under his own law. 'איש איש' adds a new case: a non-Jew who sins with a woman who is forbidden under Jewish law. Since each source has its own job, both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relationships (like a married woman or close relatives)
There / here (pointing to the two sources)

phrases.english: There, it is about their forbidden relations,
and here, it is about our forbidden relations,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means 'איש איש.' This is a non-Jew who sins with a Jewish woman, like a married Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בַּעֲרָיוֹת דִּידְהוּ, וְהָכָא בַּעֲרָיוֹת דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 about why both 'לאמר' and 'איש איש' are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases: each source teaches a different set of עריות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seem to teach the same איסור, so one looks extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לאמר' covers the non-Jews' own עריות. 'איש איש' covers Jewish עריות.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא talks about a non-Jew who sins with Jewish עריות. This shows the ברייתא does deal with that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the end of the ברייתא teaches: if he had relations with Jewish forbidden women, he is judged by Jewish law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by pointing to the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the ברייתא openly speaks about a non-Jew with Jewish עריות. So it makes sense that 'איש איש' in that ברייתא is teaching this case. The phrase 'judged by Jewish law' is unclear, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
He is judged by Jewish law

phrases.english: As the end clause teaches:
If he had relations with Jewish forbidden women,
he is judged by Jewish law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 18 with words from the ברייתא itself.
steps.raayaObject: That 'איש איש' teaches about Jewish עריות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא: 'בא על ערוות ישראל נידון בדיני ישראל.'

steps.title: What does 'judged by Jewish law' change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law is meant by 'judged by Jewish law.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next discussion. It asks what exactly changes when the non-Jew is 'judged by Jewish law.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's words are general. The גמרא wants to know which specific rule of Jewish law is applied to this non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (what difference does it make?)

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the ברייתא's phrase quoted in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical rule 'נידון בדיני ישראל' refers to.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a full court, witnesses and a warning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says it means he needs a בית דין, two witnesses and a התראה, just like a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it is needed only to teach about a court, witnesses and a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a first answer: this non-Jew is judged the same way a Jew is judged in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew to be put to death, he needs a court of judges, two kosher witnesses and a warning before the sin. רב נחמן says these same conditions apply to this non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: A court (a בית דין of judges)
A warning given before the sin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
It is needed only for the court,
and witnesses, and a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לָעֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Judged by Jewish law' means he needs a court, two witnesses and a התראה.

steps.title: That would make him better off!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: should a non-Jew who sins with a Jewish woman get an easier law than one who sins with a non-Jewish woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: Should he lose out and be treated more leniently?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's answer. His reading would make this sin easier to punish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בן נח can be put to death by one judge, on one witness, and with no warning. Adding a full court, two witnesses and a warning would make him harder to punish. It makes no sense for sinning with a Jewish woman to be treated more lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: Should it be weaker? (should he get a lighter law?)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Judged by Jewish law' sounds stricter, but here it would actually make things easier for him. A Jewish court needs more conditions before it can punish.

phrases.english: Should he lose out and be weaker?
phrases.notes: Literally 'lessening, he lessens.' The question is whether his law should become easier.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִגְרָע גָּרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that 'judged by Jewish law' means a court, witnesses and a warning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These conditions make him harder to punish than with his own עריות. A sin with Jewish עריות should not be treated more leniently.

steps.title: רב יוחנן: it is about a betrothed young girl
steps.stepSummary: רב יוחנן explains that the ברייתא is about a נערה המאורסה. Betrothal does not exist in non-Jewish law, but we judge him by our law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוחנן said: it is needed only for a betrothed young girl. That does not exist for them, so we judge them by our law.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב נחמן's answer was pushed off, the גמרא brings a new answer from רב יוחנן about what 'judged by Jewish law' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among non-Jews only full marriage counts, not אירוסין. So under his own law, being with a betrothed woman would not be adultery. With a Jewish נערה המאורסה, we use our law, and he is guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer and giving a new one)
A betrothed young girl (after אירוסין, before full marriage)

steps.whatToRemember: 'לאמר' teaches the non-Jews' own עריות, and 'איש איש' teaches Jewish עריות. 'Judged by Jewish law' means that a non-Jew who is with a Jewish נערה המאורסה is guilty, even though betrothal does not count in his own law.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that Jewish law can make a non-Jew guilty in a case that his own laws would not cover. This happens when the woman involved is Jewish.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yoḥanan said:
phrases.notes: Many versions read רבי יוחנן here.

phrases.english: It is needed only for a betrothed young girl,
which they do not have for themselves,
so we judge them by our law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹחָנָן לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְנַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב נחמן's answer, which Step 22 knocked down, with a new answer to the question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Judged by Jewish law' refers to a Jewish נערה המאורסה. He is guilty under our law, even though betrothal does not exist for non-Jews.

steps.title: Is a non-Jew who sins with a Jewish married woman judged by his own law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a non-Jew who sins with a Jewish אשת איש is judged by non-Jewish law. A ברייתא says he gets חנק. Under non-Jewish law the punishment would be סייף, so the ברייתא seems to use Jewish law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a married woman: do we judge them by their own law? Yet a ברייתא teaches: if he sinned with a betrothed young woman, he gets stoning; if with a married woman, he gets strangulation. If we used their law, it would be the sword!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a non-Jew who sins with a Jewish אשת איש is judged by non-Jewish law. It points to a ברייתא that gives him a Jewish-style punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said we only use our law for נערה המאורסה, because non-Jews have no betrothal. Non-Jews do have marriage, so for אשת איש we would expect their law, which is סייף. Yet the ברייתא says חנק, which is the Jewish punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: By their own law (the law for non-Jews)
Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
Strangulation, one of the four death penalties of בית דין

phrases.english: But a married woman,
do we judge them by their own law?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If he had relations with a betrothed young woman,
he is judged with stoning;
with a married woman, he is judged with strangulation.
And if it were by their law, it would be the sword!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, בְּדִינָא דִּידְהוּ דָּיְינִינַן לְהוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's answer and tests what it implies for אשת איש
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied rule that a case non-Jews do recognize (אשת איש) is judged by their own law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives חנק for אשת איש. That is Jewish law. Non-Jewish law would give סייף.

steps.title: The married woman in the ברייתא had entered חופה but had no relations yet
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the ברייתא is talking about a woman who entered חופה but had no relations with her husband yet. Non-Jewish law does not count her as married, so we judge him by our law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What is the 'married woman' the ברייתא teaches? A woman who entered the חופה but had no relations yet. They do not have this kind of marriage, so we judge them by our law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge. He limits the ברייתא's 'married woman' to one special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same logic as רבי יוחנן. When non-Jewish law does not recognize a status, we use our law. A woman married only through חופה is married in Jewish law but not in theirs, so the punishment is חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy, which completes the marriage in Jewish law
They do not have it (in their legal system)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What is the 'married woman' that it teaches?
For example, where she entered the wedding canopy but did not yet have relations,
which they do not have for themselves.
phrases.notes: Non-Jews have no marriage that is made only by entering the חופה.

phrases.english: So we judge them by our law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'married woman' means a regular, fully married woman, which non-Jews also recognize
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a woman married only through חופה. Non-Jews do not recognize that marriage, so Jewish law (חנק) applies

steps.title: רבי חנינא: non-Jews recognize marriage only after relations
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches that non-Jews have the status of a married woman only after relations. They have no status for a woman who entered חופה without relations. This supports רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא taught: a woman who had relations with her husband counts as married for them. A woman who entered חופה and had no relations does not count for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי חנינא as the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that non-Jews have no marriage through חופה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer depends on the claim that non-Jewish law has no marriage through חופה alone. רבי חנינא says exactly that. For non-Jews, only marriage completed by relations counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has had relations with her husband
They have it (the status exists for them)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chanina taught:
A woman who had relations with her husband: they have that,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנְסָה לְחוּפָּה וְלֹא נִבְעֲלָה – אֵין לָהֶן.
phrases.english: one who entered the wedding canopy and did not have relations: they do not have that.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the assumption behind the previous answer
steps.raayaObject: The claim that non-Jewish law has no marriage through חופה alone
steps.whatToRemember: For non-Jews, marriage counts only after relations. When a Jewish woman's status exists only in Jewish law (betrothal, or חופה without relations), a non-Jew who sins with her is judged by Jewish law.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. רבי מאיר says that a בן נח is warned about exactly those עריות for which a Jewish בית דין gives the death penalty, and no others.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: any ערוה for which a Jewish בית דין gives the death penalty, a בן נח is warned about it. One for which a Jewish בית דין does not give the death penalty, a בן נח is not warned about it. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יוחנן. It starts with רבי מאיר's rule for which עריות apply to a בן נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר links the two systems. The list of עריות forbidden to a בן נח is the same as the list of עריות that carry a death penalty in a Jewish בית דין. Anything below that level is not forbidden to a בן נח.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֶרְוָה שֶׁבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עָלֶיהָ –
phrases.english: Any forbidden relationship for which a Jewish court puts to death,
a descendant of Noah is warned about it.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עָלֶיהָ –
phrases.english: If a Jewish court does not put to death for it,
a descendant of Noah is not warned about it.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן and brings a ברייתא that supports him
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose closing clause, 'ואנו אין לנו אלא נערה המאורסה בלבד' (step 29), names נערה המאורסה as the only case where a non-Jew is judged by Jewish law, just as רבי יוחנן said

steps.title: חכמים: many עריות are forbidden to a בן נח even without a death penalty
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say there are many עריות for which a Jewish בית דין does not give the death penalty, yet a בן נח is still warned about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: there are many forbidden relationships for which a Jewish בית דין does not give the death penalty, and yet a בן נח is warned about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The second half of the ברייתא gives the view of חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים cut the link that רבי מאיר made. In their view, whether a Jewish בית דין gives the death penalty does not decide what is forbidden to a בן נח. A בן נח can be warned about more עריות than the ones that carry death in Jewish law.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבי מאיר says the list for a בן נח is exactly the list that carries death in a Jewish בית דין. חכמים say a בן נח can be warned about more than that list.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
There are many forbidden relationships

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: for which a Jewish court does not put to death,
and yet a descendant of Noah is warned about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַרְבֵּה עֲרָיוֹת יֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is warned about many עריות even when a Jewish בית דין does not give the death penalty for them

steps.title: Which law judges a non-Jew who sins with עריות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of חכמים continues. With Jewish עריות a non-Jew is judged by Jewish law, and with non-Jewish עריות by non-Jewish law. The only real case where this matters is a נערה המאורסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a non-Jew sins with forbidden Jewish women, he is judged by Jewish law. If he sins with forbidden non-Jewish women, he is judged by non-Jewish law. And we only have the case of a betrothed young woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of חכמים from the last step keeps going. It explains which court's rules decide the punishment of a non-Jew who sins with עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whose ערוה it is. A Jewish woman brings Jewish law, and a non-Jewish woman brings non-Jewish law. The ברייתא then says that the only case where Jewish law actually changes his outcome is a נערה המאורסה. That is exactly רבי יוחנן's answer in step 23, and it is why the גמרא called this ברייתא 'in agreement with רבי יוחנן'.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young woman (after אירוסין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: If he has relations with forbidden Jewish women,
he is judged by Jewish law.
If he has relations with forbidden women of בני נח,
he is judged by the law of בני נח.
And we have nothing,
phrases.notes: He means: the only case where Jewish law actually gives this non-Jew a different result.

phrases.english: except a betrothed young woman alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא עַל עֲרָיוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִידּוֹן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of חכמים begun in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jew who sins with Jewish עריות is judged by Jewish law. In practice this matters only for a נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: Why not also count a woman who entered חופה without relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא lists only a נערה המאורסה. A woman who entered חופה but had no relations should also be a case where he is judged by Jewish law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the ברייתא also count a woman who entered חופה but had no relations with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word "only" in the ברייתא. It points to another case where non-Jewish law and Jewish law seem to differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 and step 26 we learned that non-Jewish law does not count a woman as married after חופה without relations. In that case he would be judged by Jewish law too. So why does the ברייתא say the only case is a נערה המאורסה?

phrases.english: But let it also count
a woman who entered חופה but had no relations?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי נִכְנְסָה לְחוּפָּה וְלֹא נִבְעֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word בלבד in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that נערה המאורסה is the only case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Steps 25 and 26 showed that חופה without relations is also a case where non-Jews do not count her as married. So the ברייתא's list looks incomplete.

steps.title: This תנא holds that all non-Jewish death penalties are חנק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows תנא דבי מנשה, who holds that every death penalty for בני נח is חנק. Jewish law for a married woman is also חנק, so the punishment is the same either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is from the school of מנשה, who says that every death penalty stated for בני נח is only strangulation. Both this and that are strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חופה case gives no different result for this תנא. So there was no reason to list it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תנא דבי מנשה, a בן נח's death penalty is always חנק. A Jew who sins with a married woman also gets חנק. So with a woman after חופה, both systems give חנק, and only the נערה המאורסה (סקילה in Jewish law) is really different.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of the school of מנשה
This one and that one, both

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, in step 24, we assumed the non-Jewish punishment is סייף. This תנא disagrees and says it is always חנק. That is why the חופה case makes no difference here.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא counts only נערה המאורסה because it follows תנא דבי מנשה: for בני נח every death is חנק, so a married woman gives חנק under both laws.

phrases.english: This תנא
is the תנא of the school of מנשה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כׇּל מִיתָה הָאֲמוּרָה לִבְנֵי נֹחַ
phrases.english: who says: every death penalty stated for בני נח
is nothing but strangulation.
This and that are both strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא תַּנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא's view, which removes the difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חופה case should be listed because Jewish law would change the punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: For תנא דבי מנשה both laws give חנק in the חופה case, so only נערה המאורסה is a real difference.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really link a בן נח's warnings to Jewish death penalties
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי מאיר's rule from step 27. It begins to quote a ברייתא about a גר that seems to contradict him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי מאיר hold that every ערוה for which a Jewish court gives the death penalty is forbidden to a בן נח? But it was taught: a convert...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי מאיר's view and starts a challenge against it. The quoted ברייתא is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 רבי מאיר said a בן נח is warned about exactly the עריות that bring death in a Jewish court. The גמרא now brings a ברייתא about a גר to test this. The full contradiction appears only once the ברייתא is completed.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And does רבי מאיר hold:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֶרְוָה שֶׁבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: every ערוה for which a Jewish court
gives the death penalty,
a בן נח is warned about it?
But isn't it taught: a convert
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is cut off here; the rest of it comes in the next part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר כׇּל עֶרְוָה שֶׁבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עָלֶיהָ בֶּן נֹחַ מוּזְהָר עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי מאיר's view from step 27 after the side discussion about חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's rule that a בן נח is warned about exactly the עריות punished by death in a Jewish court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about a גר will be quoted that seems to go against this rule. The details continue on the next amud.
